items.title: Peak-state anchoring with probe trials
items.summary: A state's own vibration code is played at a measured peak (self-tap, HRV rise, Duchenne smile, EEG); cue-alone probe trials test whether the anchor really shifts the body.

items.title: Closed-loop sleep cueing
items.summary: Cues only in deep sleep, below waking level, stopping on arousal, with a nightly limit; the day's code replayed with light and an earbud voice; trauma gets a safety code or waking by default.

items.title: External success events and a reward code
items.summary: An outside sensor reports a success (a ball through the rim, a correct answer) and a reward code plays within a fraction of a second; it can be replayed at night.

items.title: Cue wear-out from overuse
items.summary: Every appearance of a cue outside training is counted, its loss of strength modelled, and CONTAIN warns before a cue stops working.

items.title: Generalisation score and an ordered glyph route
items.summary: Does a reaction start in many real contexts, not only the trained one; glyphs walked in ledger order as a memory route.

items.title: A code family per learning area
items.summary: Each learning area gets its own family of vibration codes, marked by a code prefix.

items.title: Phase codes in a sequence
items.summary: Each phase of a program announces itself with its own code.

items.title: Craving protocol and app or place triggers
items.summary: A craving protocol, triggered by context such as a gambling app opening or arriving at a venue.

items.title: Temperature and posture channels
items.summary: A wrist cooling device and a motion sensor for posture as cue channels.

items.title: Pronunciation feedback from the camera
items.summary: Face and lip tracking compared with a native template; moving the muscles to match is kept as a specification only. Built as sound-based feedback (melody, vowels, rhythm) with an optional camera check of mouth shape.

items.title: Anchor tree with attachment points
items.summary: A central image with three context images fixed to its parts, each with its own code; a guided recall walk with recall timed per part.

items.title: Typology chains from speech, as plug-ins
items.summary: Trait lexicons per type build a profile over a conversation; typologies are plug-ins; profiling another person needs consent.

items.title: The five-step level operator chain
items.summary: Detect, analyse, modify, output, future-pace; a classifier for which level a sentence comes from (environment to purpose); every change passes the LINX router and CONTAIN.

items.title: Therapist decision matrix and copilot
items.summary: A central meaning with three trigger cues and three responses; the therapist memorises it, the copilot runs it on a live transcript, and agreement is measured.

items.title: Display output: AR glasses and the lock screen
items.summary: A state image conditioned at peaks and shown on a trigger, in smart glasses or on the phone's lock screen.

items.title: Four-day block, voice-recognised contexts, timed burst
items.summary: A four-day acquisition block per principle; entering a real context recognised from speech or sound fires the code; a timed vibration burst.

items.title: Re-living an event with a symbol and light
items.summary: After an event, replay it in imagination with the symbol and radiant light and rehearse the new behaviour (imagery rescripting), timed and measured.

items.title: Light together with vibration
items.summary: Light comes on with the vibration so the cue is noticed more.

items.title: Content packs for any rule set
items.summary: The anchor tree as a format: any rule set, value system or skill becomes a pack.

items.title: Core Transformation protocol
items.summary: The outcome chain from an unwanted state to a core state, asked one question at a time, with a code for the core state.

items.title: The anchor triplet
items.summary: One anchor carries a vibration, a scent and a light; one scent per state; the same anchor always means the same state.

items.title: Anchor chain program type
items.summary: Anchors with roles played in sequence (healing, stability, redirection, action), each phase with its own check that it worked.

items.title: Identity profiles, level by level
items.summary: A symbol heads a tree of mission, identity, values, beliefs, skills, behaviour and environment, each level with an image and a code; the symbol by day, the whole chain at night.

items.title: A language for each identity
items.summary: Each identity learned and recalled in its own language, as a context switch between identities.

items.title: Rehearsing a value conflict
items.summary: Imagine a situation that violates a value; the body's reaction is measured and the value's anchor brings it back; future-pace the new choice.

items.title: Staged autonomy gate
items.summary: Manual training, then automatic detection, then overload conditioning, then default; an anchor may fire on its own only after it has earned it.

items.title: Vibration at the peak of the inhale
items.summary: Breathing the symbol into the chest with a posture change; the code fires at the peak of the inhale.

items.title: Peak vibration in sport via a motion sensor
items.summary: A motion sensor detects a successful move and fires the reward code.

items.title: Carrier frequency for vibration
items.summary: Vibration settings that take a carrier frequency, to test whether a frequency shifts EEG at that frequency.

items.title: Prior-art file
items.summary: Existing products and research, kept current and linked from every novelty claim.

items.title: Book outline
items.summary: A book on identity architecture, written after the prototype has data.

items.title: Glossary and foundations files
items.summary: Every term defined precisely; each module linked to the research it builds on.

items.title: Personal randomised experiments, pooled
items.summary: Single-case designs: conditions chosen at random (cue or none, real or sham anchor, automatic or manual), each person's effect with an interval, pooled across people.

items.title: The platform's identity library
items.summary: Device blueprints, ritual templates and a sequence builder exist; the identity library is missing.

items.title: Identities as user profiles
items.summary: An implant is the BIOS, the architecture is the operating system, an identity is a user profile: a login code, a global interrupt, policies per profile, timed switching.

items.title: A layer that works on any hardware
items.summary: Programs, anchors and profiles sit above the hardware; an implant device class is written as a specification only.

items.title: Versioned profiles
items.summary: As values change, the profile changes, with a record of what changed between versions.

items.title: Anchors on parts of the body
items.summary: Attachment points placed on the body; vibration motors at several places.

items.title: An environment layer for each profile
items.summary: Clothing, scent, music and the practice space prime a profile, as contexts and triggers.

items.title: Recovery and override metrics
items.summary: Overrides per day, the share of fear events turned around, reaction time under stress, memory under fatigue.

items.title: Perceptual-event triggers
items.summary: Unusual perceptual states as a trigger type, always routed through CONTAIN's escalation path.

items.title: An identity layer for AI agents and robots
items.summary: An agent loads a profile, simulates an action against its values before acting, overrides on a conflict and logs whether each action matched its values; CONTAIN enforces it.

items.title: People and machines signalling through glyphs
items.summary: An agent reports its state as a glyph's code on the wristband; the person replies with a code.

items.title: Human error and stress signals feeding the agent
items.summary: A person's error-related or stress signal sharpens the agent's conflict detector.

items.title: Behaviour-consistency test
items.summary: How consistent an agent's behaviour is with a profile and without one.

items.title: Provenance of names, manifesto and briefs
items.summary: Every name kept with who coined it; one-page briefs for scientists, therapists and other audiences.

items.title: Life-timeline memory protocol
items.summary: Scattered life events mapped into ordered nodes with glyphs (memory specificity training).

items.title: Built-in cognitive tests
items.summary: n-back, digit span, reaction time under stress, event recall, reading and threat-attention bias, dated over time.

items.title: Lifestyle factors as background data
items.summary: Nutrition, cold exposure and similar factors logged as covariates in personal trials, not as advice.

items.title: DOL-9, the daily override loop, and OXQ
items.summary: A precise 90-second loop (breath 4-2-6, posture, phrase, gesture, 5-15 s action) as an RSX program; OXQ = overrides / waking hours x 100.

items.title: Four-step sequence, layers in another language, a month's dose
items.summary: On a negative state: identity peak, Core Transformation, future-pacing, movement-peak vibrations; six layers practised in another language; 12 a day for a month.

items.title: Trial: Core Transformation first or identity first
items.summary: The order question settled by a randomised crossover.

items.title: Four orders as trial arms
items.summary: The three-phase hybrid, Core Transformation first in each cycle, the identity peak first, and identity fully first.

items.title: Typology network and mirroring drift
items.summary: Type image, common phrases, responses; does mirroring others pull a person away from their own profile.

items.title: A prepared identity week for clients
items.summary: One level a day for seven days with future-pacing, then the symbol installed in trance and three future situations.

items.title: Dual-use governance
items.summary: A consent record for any profiling, an audit log, and a visible flag on anything that works below awareness.

items.title: Trigger atlas
items.summary: A week of mapping which objects, sounds, smells, places and thoughts shift state, as a weighted graph with baselines, repeats, controls and statistics on each link.

items.title: Real-time rerouting
items.summary: When a high-weight trigger appears, the good-state anchor fires as vibration and scent, through the gate.

items.title: Smell sensor and combined trigger nodes
items.summary: Gas sensors that classify smells; a sound with one object may trigger a state while the same sound with another may not, so the graph models combinations.

items.title: Network trance with a transfer test
items.summary: Every way one feeling arrives across the senses; in trance, transform the biggest node and watch the change spread; reactivity on untreated nodes is the test; compared with Time Line Therapy.

items.title: Whole-day sampling and map readiness
items.summary: Smells, tastes, thoughts, symbols, objects and feelings sampled across the day; how many exposures each node needs before its weight is stable.

items.title: Genealogy timeline in four eras
items.summary: 2023 mnemonic images; April 2025 EEG, vibration and senses; May 2025 identity trees and sequences; July 2025 the atlas and the network trance.

items.title: The transfer engine
items.summary: Choose the node to work on by weight (across the senses) or by level (above the problem), then measure transfer to nodes never treated.

items.title: SSIT three-arm trial
items.summary: Imagery about the activity, imagery about a higher node flowing down, and general calming imagery; transfer to untrained activities as the outcome.

items.title: Library of higher nodes and a level sweep
items.summary: Ten candidate nodes above language; does transfer rise, peak or fall as the node gets more abstract, per person.

items.title: Anchor contamination and restoration
items.summary: An anchor used during an ongoing stressor can take on the stress; detect when its effect turns negative and restore it by pairing with a higher-order resource.

items.title: Two kinds of higher: abstraction and scope
items.summary: Higher by abstraction (language, agency, identity) and higher by scope (a city, a country), tested side by side.

items.title: A two-symbol anchor
items.summary: Two symbols held together as one anchor, the same form as the Tier 013 composite.

items.title: A setting that prepares the state
items.summary: Warmth, music and imagery logged with each session so personal trials can show whether the setting matters.

combinations.title: Anchors you can program and measure
combinations.summary: Anchors are captured at a measured peak, composed into chains, tested with probes, checked for contamination and restored.

combinations.title: One conditioning loop around the clock
combinations.summary: Anchoring by day, firing on triggers, reactivation at night, wear-out monitoring and personal trials.

combinations.title: A device that limits its own autonomy
combinations.summary: It earns the right to act by itself, one anchor at a time.

combinations.title: Map, intervene, remap
combinations.summary: The session is written from a person's own trigger graph, and the change in that graph is the outcome.

combinations.title: One program, two executors
combinations.summary: The therapist memorises the matrix and the copilot runs it; the system measures where they agree and differ.

combinations.title: One format for people and machines
combinations.summary: The same value tree gates an agent's actions and builds a person's identity.

combinations.title: One lineage engine for the design records and for a person
combinations.summary: The trigger atlas has the same graph structure as the genealogy of the design records: the same operators on two different materials.

hypotheses.title: A central node spreads its change, and this held across every form
hypotheses.evidence: 2023 central image; the anchor tree; the network trance; SSIT. Product-side test in step 5 (transfer to untreated nodes).

hypotheses.title: Setbacks come before structural leaps
hypotheses.evidence: A collapse, then the device architecture; discouragement, then the operating-system analogy.

hypotheses.title: A probe becomes a rule, then default behaviour
hypotheses.evidence: A challenge to an unsupported claim (May 2025), then a standing rule against exceptionalism in prompts (July 2025), then calibrated assistants and this claims register.

hypotheses.title: A class of claims with numbers but no data
hypotheses.evidence: Scores, ranks, thresholds and timelines given without measurement; count them and trace what each set off.

hypotheses.title: Re-entry events
hypotheses.evidence: Assistant text reused as the seed of a later design record (records 17, 34, 38).

hypotheses.title: The lion and dragon thread
hypotheses.evidence: An emoji row in 2025 records, then Tier 013 (🦁 + 🐉), the lion and the dragon held as one composite.
